findings.title: record_for_host returns false instead of nil, creating inconsistent return types
findings.body: The method `record_for_host` returns `false` (a boolean) when the URI is invalid or the host is blank, but returns an ActiveRecord object or `nil` from the query otherwise. This inconsistent return type is error-prone. In `topic_embed.rb` it's used as `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` followed by `eh.try(:category_id)`. While `try` happens to handle `false` gracefully (returning nil since FalseClass doesn't respond to `category_id`), any future caller using a simple nil-check (`if record_for_host(url)`) would get unexpected truthy behavior from `false`. The method should return `nil` instead of `false` for consistency.

findings.title: No nil check on record lookup in update and destroy actions
findings.body: In both `update` (line 10) and `destroy` (line 15), `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return `nil` if the record doesn't exist. In `update`, `save_host(nil)` will raise `NoMethodError` when calling `host.host = ...`. In `destroy`, `host.destroy` will similarly raise. This results in a 500 error instead of a proper 404 response. The controller should either use `find` (which raises RecordNotFound and is handled by Rails) or add an explicit nil check.

findings.title: SQL injection via string interpolation of user-controlled data in migration
findings.body: The migration interpolates the variable `h` (which comes from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting, a value that admins can set to arbitrary strings) directly into a SQL string: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. If the stored value contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacters, this will either break the migration or allow SQL injection. Use parameterized queries or at minimum `quote(h)` / `connection.quote(h)` to escape the value.

findings.title: Migration will crash if embed_category site setting doesn't exist
findings.body: The query on lines 9-11 joins `categories` with `site_settings` where `s.name = 'embed_category'`. If the `embed_category` site setting was never configured (which is the default empty-string case), the INNER JOIN returns zero rows. Accessing `[0]['id']` on an empty result set raises `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass`, causing the migration to fail. The code should handle the case where the query returns no rows.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped with their filenames
findings.body: The file `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `embeddable_host` fabricator, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. The file contents are inverted relative to their names. While Fabrication loads all files in the directory regardless of name, this is confusing for maintainers and could cause issues if any tooling or convention relies on filename-to-content correspondence.

findings.title: before_validation callback will raise NoMethodError if host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` which will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` if `self.host` is nil. This can happen if a new `EmbeddableHost` is validated before the host attribute is assigned, or if the host parameter is missing/nil in the controller. The callback should guard against nil, e.g., `self.host&.sub!(...)` or check for presence first.
